newsitem.title: USA: Astra USA ordered to arbitrate complaint.
newsitem.headline: Astra USA ordered to arbitrate complaint.

text.p: A federal judge ordered Astra USA and a former employee who has accused three executives of the pharmaceutical company of sexual harassment to arbitrate their differences, company officials said Thursday.
U.S. District Judge Edward Harrington ruled late Tuesday in favour of a motion filed by Astra USA to submit the dispute to an independent third-party arbitrator, according to court documents.

"We're pleased with the result," Astra USA spokesman Benjamin Kincannon told Reuters. "Arbitration is something that is used increasingly by American companies as an important way to resolve employee suits."

Melanie Strobel, a former sales trainee for the company, alleged that Astra USA's former chief executive officer and two other executives engaged in sexual harassment and created a "hostile and oppressive work environment" which led to severe emotional distress.
The three men have denied any wrongdoing.
Strobel's lawyer, Philip Giordano, said they may appeal the judge's decision.

Former Chief Executive Officer Lars Bildman of Astra USA, a unit of Swedish pharmaceutical firm Astra Ab, was fired last year after an internal investigation of alleged sexual harassment and financial improprieties. Bildman has been held in jail without bail since April when he was arrested on 35 charges, including fraud and tax evasion.
